tool.name: Trackastra CTC export
tool.description: prepare tracked masks and lineage data for Napari and external CTC tools
tool.command: mkdir -p 'ctc_masks' && #for $i, $mask in enumerate($tracked_masks): #set $frame = '%04d' % $i ln -s '$mask' 'ctc_masks/man_track${frame}.tiff' && #end for python '$__tool_directory__/ctc_to_napari.py' --track-table '$track_table' --masks-dir 'ctc_masks' --tracks-out 'napari_tracks.csv' --graph-out 'napari_graph.json' --stack-out 'napari_tracked_stack.tiff' --ctc-dir 'ctc_output'

param.name: track_table
param.label: CTC track table
param.help: The Trackastra man_track.txt output containing track ID, start frame, end frame, and parent track ID.

param.name: tracked_masks
param.label: Tracked CTC masks
param.help: Ordered Trackastra mask collection. Collection order defines time and must begin at frame 0.

tool.help:
**Trackastra CTC export** converts the standard Trackastra outputs into files that can be viewed in Galaxy's Napari interactive tool and exchanged with other Cell Tracking Challenge software.
Inputs ======
- A CTC ``man_track.txt`` table from Trackastra. - The ordered tracked-mask TIFF collection from the same Trackastra job. Elements may carry either the ``tiff`` or the ``tif`` datatype.
Outputs =======
- **Napari image stack**: a single multi-page ``tiff`` holding every tracked mask with time as the leading axis, so Napari opens one layer with a time slider instead of one layer per frame. The tracks table and the lineage graph are also embedded in the TIFF description, which means this one dataset carries everything needed to build a Tracks layer. - **Napari tracks CSV**: one row per tracked object observation, with columns ``track_id,t,y,x`` for 2D data or ``track_id,t,z,y,x`` for 3D data. Rows are sorted by track ID and time in the order Napari's Tracks layer expects. - **Napari lineage graph JSON**: maps each child track ID to its parent track ID list. - **CTC masks**: a list collection of the validated masks under canonical ``man_trackNNNN`` element identifiers. Downloading the collection yields ``man_trackNNNN.tiff`` files; place the ``man_track.txt`` input dataset next to them to obtain a complete Cell Tracking Challenge directory.
Viewing the results in Galaxy =============================
The **Run Napari** interactive tool accepts image datasets only. Its ``Images`` parameter is restricted to ``jpg``, ``png``, ``tiff``, ``bmp``, ``gif``, ``pcx``, ``ppm``, ``psd``, ``pbm``, ``pgm``, ``eps``, and ``spatialdata.zip``, so the tracks CSV and the lineage JSON cannot be selected there. Use the **Napari image stack** output instead:
1. Run **Perform object tracking with Trackastra** to obtain the CTC track table and the tracked-mask collection. 2. Run this export tool on those two outputs. 3. Rename the resulting Napari image stack in the history to something short, such as ``tracks``. The interactive tool stages each dataset under its history name, so a long name becomes an awkward filename inside the viewer. 4. Launch **Run Napari** and select the Napari image stack as the image. The stack opens as a single layer with a time slider.
Anything saved into the ``output`` directory inside the interactive tool is returned to the history as a collection when the job ends.
Notes on the other outputs ==========================
The CSV, JSON, and CTC mask outputs are download and interoperability artifacts, not interactive-tool inputs. They suit desktop Napari, TrackMate, Mastodon, and the Cell Tracking Challenge evaluation software.
